summary: John Brockington is an Indologist. He held posts at the University of Edinburgh, where he was attested as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit in 1987 and as Professor of Sanskrit from 1998 to 2003.

John Brough was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and at St John's College, Cambridge, under Harold Walter Bailey. He held professorships at the University of London (1948–1967) and Cambridge (1967–1984).
John Buescher works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982, and was attested as Director at the Voice of America in 2001.

John Burnet was a scholar of philosophy. He studied at the Royal High School, the University of Edinburgh, and Balliol College, Oxford. He spent the majority of his academic career at the University of St Andrews from circa 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page was an Indologist, archaeologist, and linguist. He studied at the Royal College of Music and the University of Oxford. His academic career included appointments at SOAS University of London (circa 1954–1984) and Deccan College (circa 1958–1960).

John C. Huntington was an art historian, Tibetologist, and scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Ohio State University, with his tenure attested between 1987 and 1990 as well as in 2000.

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He was affiliated with the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and later as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1790 to 1797 and was appointed professor of Hindustani at Fort William College in 1808.

John Chadwick was a linguist and classical archaeologist. He studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, worked on the Oxford Latin Dictionary (circa 1946–1952), and served at the University of Cambridge as a lecturer and Reader in Classics (1969–1984).

John Claude White was active in Tibetology and archaeology. He studied at Rugby School and the Royal Indian Engineering College before serving as an Assistant Engineer in the Bengal Public Works Department from 1876.

John Clifford Holt is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He was Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (circa 1978–2020).

John Collinson Nesfield was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Merton College, Oxford. He taught at Highgate School, Krishnagar Government College, and Presidency College, Chennai, and served as principal of Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi, in 1878.

John Corrigan is a religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago and held positions at Harvard, the University of Virginia, and Arizona State University before joining Florida State University around 2001 as a distinguished professor.
John Crawfurd was an archaeologist and linguist. He studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1800 to 1803 and worked as a doctor for the East India Company from 1803 to 1808.

John Crook was a researcher in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Southampton and Cambridge, completing his doctorate under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe. He was appointed at the University of Bristol in 1977.

John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel. He taught at Emory University (circa 2005–2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

John D. Smith is an Indologist and linguist. He was a lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London in 1975 before moving to the University of Cambridge, where he served as Lecturer (1984) and Professor (2001–2007).

John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Rutgers University and under Taizan Maezumi and Soen Nakagawa. He taught at Naropa University in 1974 and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from circa 1980 to 2009.
John Daishin Buksbazen is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman, as attested in 2002.

John Dewey was an American philosopher. He studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan, the University of Minnesota, the University of Chicago (circa 1894–1904), and Columbia University (circa 1904–1930).
